title: Knowledge check: Creating Your First Express.js Project

questions.prompt: In Creating Your First Express.js Project, which statement best describes Initializing a Node.js project?
options: Define acceptance criteria before coding, integrate one vertical slice at a time, and verify the result with a repeatable test and a clear rollback/cleanup plan.

Connect this syllabus point to Creating Your First Express.js Project: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
questions.answer_key: Define acceptance criteria before coding, integrate one vertical slice at a time, and verify the result with a repeatable test and a clear rollback/cleanup plan.
questions.explanation: Define acceptance criteria before coding, integrate one vertical slice at a time, and verify the result with a repeatable test and a clear rollback/cleanup plan.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Creating Your First Express.js Project?
options: Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

A dependable project starts with a supported Node.js runtime, a lockfile, explicit module-system choices, and repeatable npm scripts. Run the same startup command from a clean checkout and record version assumptions.
questions.answer_key: A dependable project starts with a supported Node.js runtime, a lockfile, explicit module-system choices, and repeatable npm scripts. Run the same startup command from a clean checkout and record version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A dependable project starts with a supported Node.js runtime, a lockfile, explicit module-system choices, and repeatable npm scripts. Run the same startup command from a clean checkout and record version assumptions.

questions.prompt: A change related to Creating Your First Express.js Project appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
